city-desc.default	You can create a custom city. Click 'Continue' to see full customization options.
city-desc.chicago	<i>The Windy City</i> was often at the center of conflict over Prohibition in the United States. Located on Lake Michigan at the crossroads of the nation's railways, and overflowing with wealthy industrialists and poor immigrant workforce, the city was infamous for its blatant defiance of dry laws and profiting off of illegal alcohol sales. Many famous criminal organizations clashed on its streets including Al Capone's Outfit and Dean O'Banion's North Side Gang.\n\nIn Chicago booze flows freely, but starting locations are not all made equal. Downtown is reasonably accessible from almost anywhere, however the highest concentration of industrial areas and train stations will be located around the Back of the Yards and West Loop which may require some creative relationship management to gain access to. Bridges are a key feature and link the three main regions, but provide opportunities for rivals to block off important routes.
city-desc.detroit	<i>The Motor City</i> has long been renowned for its booming automobile industry. Desiring a sober workforce, Henry Ford famously backed the Damon act of 1918, which was a precursor to the eighteenth amendment. But as the sale of alcohol remained legal in Canada throughout prohibition, neighboring Windsor, Ontario became a hotspot for alcohol smuggling. The Purple Gang, a criminal mob of bootleggers and hijackers, were perhaps Detroit's most notorious gang, going as far as supplying Canadian whiskey to Al Capone's Chicago Outfit.\n\nThe Detroit river separates the city from its Canadian neighbor of Windsor, Ontario. A lack of bridges means that there is no conventional access between the two cities, however the river does provide scope for smuggling across the border via boat. If you work your relationships and build some trust with Canadians living in Detroit you will have the opportunity to fund an agent and safehouse over the border. You can then transfer money and resources to this new safehouse and utilize your Canadian crew member to procure <i>Canadian whiskey,</i> a unique alcohol resource that can be sold back in Detroit for a tidy profit. 
city-desc.pittsburgh	At the start of prohibition, the <i>Steel City</i> was both an industrial powerhouse and a melting pot of European nationals. Partly as a result of the cultural significance of alcohol for many of its migrant workers, Pittsburgh was soon declared the 'wettest spot in the United States' by prohibition leaders. Sicilian and Neapolitan crime families fought bitterly over territory in the north and south of the city.\n\nPittsburgh is home to two unique drinks: <i>applejack</i> and <i>rakija</i>. With these two additional alcohol types, this city has a much larger and more diverse market for alcohol than the other cities, meaning that it will be easier to get a faster start and earn more money overall. However, the three rivers and abundant hills create a ton of choke points which could present you with challenges when expanding your territory, so you'll need to be extra careful with where you set up your fronts and how you work your relationships.
city-desc.cincinnati	Before prohibition, the <i>Queen City</i> had a proud heritage of beer brewing and corn whiskey distilling, with neighboring Kentucky providing an ample supply of the world famous bourbon. The lawyer and pharmacist turned bootlegger, George Remus built his criminal empire around a loophole in the Volstead act which allowed him to repurpose distilleries to produce bonded alcohol. He was then able to sell this alcohol for 'medicinal purposes' through an extensive network of pharmacies.\n\nIn Cincinnati you'll have access to corn as a new ingredient for moonshine and the city's famed <i>corn whiskey.</i> But once you manage to get access to <i>Kentucky bourbon,</i> you will be able to command much higher prices, by selling it to highly demanding bootlegger, speakeasies, and clubs.
city-desc.atlantic-city	During Prohibition, <i>America's Playground</i> was a haven for bootlegging and gambling. The tourist economy of Atlantic City created high demand for entertainment and alcohol while its coastal location provided a perfect setting for booze smuggling.\n\nIn Atlantic City you will have greater freedom when building up your gambling operations, including unique opportunities such as luxury casinos and high stakes games. You'll also learn about lucrative new alcohol types such as Scotch Whiskey and Caribbean Rum among others from local ethnic groups scattered around the map.\n\nThe loosely connected patchwork of neighboring towns separated by a tangle of bays and estuaries will provide interesting geographic challenges, so you'll need to expand your relationship network carefully if you want to gain access to the industrial centres and train stations located in nearby Northfield and Egg Harbor.
city-desc.philadelphia	At the confluence of the Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers, William Penn's <i>City of Brotherly Love</i> was founded in 1682 as a beacon for tolerance and freedom. This cradle of American independence extended this tolerance into Prohibition. Before the Volstead act came into effect in 1921, there were an estimated 1,700 saloons laced through Philadelphia's street and neighborhoods. By 1930, estimates were that roughly 1,200 still existed more or less in the open.\n\nPhilly's famous bootleggers like Max �Boo Boo� Hoff and Mickey Duffy were key players in the East Coast booze trade, brining illegal alcohol up from the New Jersey coast and along road and rail networks from the city's rural hinterlands. And they became staggeringly rich from the industrial alcohol produced in the Delaware Valley's sprawling chemical industry. So wealthy did Max Hoff become that he founded numerous financial institutions such as the infamous Franklin Mortgage & Investment Company, a money laundering front for what became the most lucrative bootlegging operation in the USA.\n\nAll of this fills the streets of Philadelphia with huge variety of schemes to pursue once your outfit has the captains to do it. Use the homemade brandy that you can manufacture and build up a new criminal empire.\n\n<b>So large are the opportunities here, you'll need some help. Outfits in Philadelphia start with a second crew member - a seasoned captain to help you take over Pennsylvania's largest city.</b>
city-desc.new-york	Welcome to the <i>Big Apple,</i> home of a corrupt political machine the likes of which the world has never seen. It's an ideal spot to get into politics with your outfit's ill-gotten gains as you expand across Brooklyn, Bronx, Queens, and Manhattan.\n\nHidden behind the distinctive buildings and iconic landmarks of New York City are opportunities unique to this most ritzy and roaring of cities. Access the bustling ports and rail terminals around the city�s booming harbor, make copious amounts of moonshine, and craft luxury liquors to grace the cocktail menus of the city�s swankiest watering holes. Then turn your attention to politics and make sure that everybody on the council knows which side their bread is buttered � and use your newfound powers to buttress your own business and break the competition.\n\nThe expansive city map is full of great opportunity and even greater competition. Are you ready to stand up to the challenge, and add your outfit to the illustrious list of New York City's criminal elite?
